Environment-specific genetic covariance (experimental)

Source: R/fit_G_env.R
fit_G_env.Rd

Estimates the genetic covariance of a set of traits within and between the groups of a discrete environment (sex, diet, site), treating each trait in each environment as its own trait ("character states"). Each individual is observed only in its own environment, so the genetic covariance between environments is identified through relatives in different environments, and the residual covariance between environments is not identified at all: it is zero by construction.

Usage

fit_G_env(Y, env, X = NULL, A, engine = "sommer", ...)

Arguments

Y

Numeric matrix, individuals by traits.

env

The environment of each individual: a vector or factor with one value per row of Y and at least two levels, or the name of a column of X.

X, A

As for fit_G().

engine

Block engine; "sommer" by default (the stanimal engine imputes every unobserved character state and is much slower here). "wombat" holds the unidentified residual covariances between environments at zero instead of estimating them.

...

Passed to fit_G().

Value

An object of class indri_fit_env: G and E (character states by character states, in the units of Y), corr_between (traits by pairs of environments: each trait's genetic correlation between two environments), levels, traits, states (the character-state names), env (each individual's environment, named by individual) and fit (the fit_G() fit of the character states). Pass it to indri_gwas() as fit to scan with this covariance.

Details

The response is reshaped to one column per trait and environment ("trait:level"), each observed only in that environment's individuals, and fit_G() fits it with its usual assembly and engines. Unless subsets, s or min_cooccurrence is given, the subsets are trait-paired: one block per pair of traits, holding both traits in every environment (P (P - 1) / 2 blocks of 2 L states for P traits in L environments; fit_G()'s usual subsets for fewer than three traits). Each cross-environment covariance is then estimated in every block that holds the trait, next to its own within-environment variances. G is the assembled genetic covariance of the character states: its diagonal blocks are the within-environment G and its off-diagonal blocks the genetic covariance between environments (a cross-environment genetic correlation below 1 is genotype-by-environment interaction in the background). E is block diagonal: within each environment, the residual covariance of the traits after X minus that environment's block of G (scaled for the relatedness within it), floored like fit_G()'s E.

The environment's main effect is carried by the character states' own means, so a column of X named by env is dropped; every other column of X must vary within each environment.

This is a trial: the cross-environment covariances rest on relatives in different environments only. In simulations (900 sibs of both sexes, 10 and 30 traits; STATUS.md) fit_G()'s usual subsets gave cross-environment genetic correlations too low (0.67-0.77 where the truth was 1, 0.38-0.45 where it was 0.5): most blocks held a trait in one environment only, and the projection onto a positive semi-definite G pulled the few cross-environment entries towards zero. Trait-paired subsets give 0.84-0.85 and 0.49-0.50. Scans with this covariance (indri_gwas() with this fit) remain somewhat conservative for interaction tests (genomic inflation 0.91-0.99), not anti-conservative.
